sources.label: LegislationPatch site-facts sheet — countable claims derived from the repository by scripts/generate-site-facts.js
scripts/fetch_bills_data.js — bill metadata and text fetch
scripts/fetch-reference.js — referenced statute and manual fetcher
scripts/fetch_cr_data.js — Congressional Record fetch via GovInfo
scripts/fetch_bill_cr.js — bill-page quote extraction and its verbatim check
scripts/fetch_vote_data.js — roll-call fetch and crossover detection
scripts/prompts.js — drafting prompts and quality rules
scripts/lib/article-ledger.js — how an article receipt binds to one named source

claims.claim: Bill metadata — sponsor, cosponsors, committee referrals, action history — comes from the Congress.gov API.
claims.sourceSpan: https://api.congress.gov/v3/bill/${CONGRESS_SESSION}/${type.toLowerCase()}/${number}?format=json&api_key=${CONGRESS_API_KEY}

claims.claim: Bill text comes from that same Congress.gov API.
claims.sourceSpan: https://api.congress.gov/v3/bill/${congress}/${type.toLowerCase()}/${number}/text?format=json&api_key=${CONGRESS_API_KEY}

claims.claim: The newest applicable version is preferred: enrolled, then engrossed amendment, engrossed, reported, and only then introduced.
claims.sourceSpan: (Enrolled > Engrossed Amendment > Engrossed > Reported > Introduced), tie-broken

claims.claim: Only 68 of the 219 bills in the database have been signed into law, so most do not show enrolled text.
claims.sourceSpan: Bills signed into law (stage signed), and so eligible to show enrolled text: 68 of 219

claims.claim: The stored text can lag: 73 of the 151 non-enacted bills show an older version than Congress.gov now lists, and 2 of the 68 enacted ones still show the text as introduced.
claims.sourceSpan: Bills whose stored text is OLDER than the newest version their own versions[] lists as posted: 73 of 151 non-enacted bills.

claims.claim: A statute a bill amends is fetched separately and stored before a figure is drawn from it.
claims.sourceSpan: It saves the source text to data/ref-text/

claims.claim: The Congressional Record is fetched from GovInfo.
claims.sourceSpan: https://api.govinfo.gov/packages/${packageId}/granules/${granuleId}/htm?api_key=${GOVINFO_API_KEY}

claims.claim: The U.S. Code and chamber manuals are fetched from GovInfo too.
claims.sourceSpan: --rule pulls a standing chamber rule from the House Rules and Manual (govinfo HMAN)

claims.claim: Every sentence of a stored quote has to appear verbatim in the fetched text or the quote is discarded.
claims.sourceSpan: // Every sentence of the quote must appear verbatim in the CR

claims.claim: The analysis records what a bill adds, removes, or alters relative to existing law.
claims.sourceSpan: added = new programs or rights created by this bill

claims.claim: The sponsor, party, state and cosponsor count are recorded, and whether support crossed party lines.
claims.sourceSpan: Cite: current chamber majority, sponsor party, cosponsor count

claims.claim: Crossovers are flagged only where the margin is within 30% of total yeas plus nays.
claims.sourceSpan: if (Math.abs(yeas - nays) / total > 0.30) return [];

claims.claim: Vote data comes from the House Clerk and Senate roll-call archives.
claims.sourceSpan: // clerk.house.gov/evs/{year}/roll{N}.xml

claims.claim: Passage likelihood is the one field where broader political reasoning is permitted, and it is a judgment call rather than a model output.
claims.sourceSpan: the only zone where broader political reasoning is permitted

claims.claim: Training data and unsourced prior knowledge are not admissible; a claim that cannot be tied to a stored source line is deleted.
claims.sourceSpan: A claim you cannot tie to a stored source line is DELETED, not hedged, not softened.

claims.claim: The validator runs 27 check sections.
claims.sourceSpan: Check sections in validate-batch.js: 27

claims.claim: Fourteen of those sections can block a release.
claims.sourceSpan: Sections that can block a release (call fail()): 14

claims.claim: Thirteen sections only warn.
claims.sourceSpan: Sections that only warn: 13

claims.claim: Among the blocking checks are bill-text presence, referenced-source resolution, quote quality, and stage-versus-vote consistency.
claims.sourceSpan: Blocking sections: Unprocessed bills; Required fields; Bill text files;

claims.claim: The figure-sourcing guard warns rather than blocks, and blocks only under the opt-in strict flag.
claims.sourceSpan: it blocks only under the opt-in --strict flag.

claims.claim: A strict run turns every remaining warning into a blocking error.
claims.sourceSpan: const blocking = errors > 0 || (STRICT && warnings > 0);

claims.claim: A warning must be fixed, re-sourced, or recorded in a tracked adjudication file with the evidence.
claims.sourceSpan: data/qa-adjudications.json

claims.claim: The re-read is claim-atomic: each proposition is judged supported by a quoted span, contradicted, or unsupported.
claims.sourceSpan: **SUPPORTED** (quote the verbatim span — no span, it is NOT supported), **CONTRADICTED**, or **UNSUPPORTED**

claims.claim: The re-read targets direction-of-change errors among others.
claims.sourceSpan: polarity/direction

claims.claim: The model that performed the audit is recorded on the ledger.
claims.sourceSpan: "auditModel": "opus",               // finder (or *-import for seeds)

claims.claim: No bill ledger records which model drafted the analysis, so the site does not claim of a bill analysis that a different model audited what wrote it.
claims.sourceSpan: Bill ledgers recording a drafting model at all: 0 of 212

claims.claim: Each analysis retains a per-bill record of the claims examined and the source line each was verified against.
claims.sourceSpan: write `data/qa-ledger/{id}.json` per audited bill

claims.claim: An explainer fetches and stores its authority before drafting.
claims.sourceSpan: Fetch first, draft second.

claims.claim: An article claim is bound to a verbatim span of ONE named stored source; pooled verification does not exist for articles.
claims.sourceSpan: source (`sourceFile`) and is checked against THAT FILE ONLY.

claims.claim: A bill may appear in an explainer only as a receipt-bound factual example, never as analysis or a position.
claims.sourceSpan: Bill material is allowed ONLY as receipt-bound factual examples

claims.claim: An article with any open flag on its ledger cannot be published.
claims.sourceSpan: open flag(s) still on the ledger — converge the audit first

claims.claim: The publishing script refuses an article whose ledger names the same model as drafter and auditor.
claims.sourceSpan: are the same model family

claims.claim: The publish is a human decision: the script does not commit, push, or ping anything.
claims.sourceSpan: It does NOT commit, push, or ping IndexNow

claims.claim: 107 bills are on an explicit not-analyzed list.
claims.sourceSpan: Bills deliberately excluded from analysis in data/analysis-skip.json: 107

claims.claim: That list covers ceremonial measures, House housekeeping, minor bills deferred for later, and resolutions of disapproval.
claims.sourceSpan: Excluded bills by category: 29 ceremonial, 28 deferred-minor, 27 procedural, 23 cra-disapproval

claims.claim: Each analysis records the date it was written, and a stage that moved after that date is flagged for re-review.
claims.sourceSpan: section('Analysis freshness (analyzedAt)');
